result.edited:
The human plateau shifted. The posts spread through feeds like wildfire: it was prime time, just before the end of the workday. Two hundred thousand viewers instantly jumped to two hundred and fifty thousand. Online media bots picked up the event and began circulating news about the provocative stream of “the most innovative business coach of our generation.” And a woman, no less!

Now 350,000 people from around the world were watching, liking, sharing, and paying real dollars to ask Freya questions. Three hundred and sixty thousand. Three hundred and seventy thousand. With every new thousand Freya's breath caught. And then it was time to answer.

The main thing was not to let this conversation with subscribers turn into a group date on Tinder.

“Do you have children?” asked a stranger. “How do you achieve success when you have four of them?”

Freya wanted to answer, “You don't.” But, first, moms on maternity leave made up forty-eight percent of her audience, so the question was a sore spot. And second, you couldn't answer a subscriber that way, especially one who had most likely scraped together those fifty bucks from the money meant for her kids' school lunches. So Freya gave a polite, rehearsed answer.

“Everyone defines success for themselves,” she said. “If you have always dreamed of being a mom or a dad, then your children *are* your capital. The key is to stick to an investment strategy and not put your capital into unproven funds.”

“Are you married?” someone asked, after donating the minimum five dollars.

Freya had been leaving such questions unanswered. Luckily, the flow of more interesting (and more expensive!) questions washed all the cheap provocations down the drain.

Besides, her joke had landed. The chat was delighted, and the viewer count kept growing: the clip with her answer had already gone viral on Twitter. But fame comes with responsibility, and the questions abruptly veered into the genre of a Tinder group date.
